theme: Growing one big crystal instead of many small ones
title: Batch Cooling Crystallizer: Cool Schedule and Seed Choice Under a Steepening Solubility Curve
strategies: trivial: dump straight to T_min on step 1 and hold it there (maximum instantaneous supersaturation) with the smallest seed option -- the checker's own reference construction; detonates the nucleation term and yields fine powder

greedy: constant-rate (linear) cooling from T_start to T_min, seeded with whichever option has the most total surface area -- a reasonable-sounding recipe that ignores the shape of the solubility curve and rushes through its steep bottom slice late, with little batch time left for the resulting nuclei to grow

strong: exploits the fact that the given solubility curve is steep near T_min and nearly flat near T_start -- reduces the intractable full-schedule search to a 2D grid over (seed option, a single cooling-rate-falls-over-time shape exponent p<1) simulated with the checker's own population-balance model, entering the steep region early while most of the batch time still remains for growth to consume the released solute
invalid: out-of-range seed index plus a schedule that heats above T_start before ever cooling -- rejected before scoring
